MARKET.head: Seven US regions seek AVA status to establish wine identity
MARKET.summ: From Minnesota to New Jersey, seven proposed AVAs aim to distinguish emerging regions by climate, soils, and grape varieties
takeaways: Seven proposed AVAs span California, Oregon, New Jersey, and New York; approval by the federal Alcohol and Tobacco Tax and Trade Bureau typically takes several years.
Annapolis-Sea Ranch in Sonoma County will cover 26,637 acres with 651 acres planted, known for Pinot Noir and Chardonnay shaped by coastal fog and Ohlson Ranch soil.
Deschutes River in central Oregon will be the state's first recognized winegrowing region at 723,760 acres, with growers testing both traditional European varieties and cold-hardy hybrids.

MARKET.head: Airlines upgrade wine service as premiumization strategy takes flight
MARKET.summ: Nota Bene is a periodic Wine Economist column that briefly highlights stories that might otherwise escape attention. This month we focus on good news stories about wine and wine markets. This isn’t an attempt to paper over the industry’s troubles and challenges.
takeaways: Major carriers including Delta are expanding wine offerings in premium cabins and lounges as part of broader premiumization strategies to drive profit from higher-fare seats.
The timing favors wine suppliers: airlines can source quality wines at favorable prices while positioning wine as central to aspirational lifestyle offerings.
Chateau Ste. Michelle's new ownership by the Wyckoff family signals investment confidence in Washington wine, while the Auction of Washington Wines raised over four million dollars this year.

MARKET.head: Cruise lines emerge as experiential sales channel for US wineries
MARKET.summ: From dedicated charters to custom bottlings, wineries are leveraging cruise partnerships to capture engaged audiences and drive long-term sales
takeaways: Cooper's Hawk Winery & Restaurant chartered Virgin Voyages' Valiant Lady for its wine club in 2026, integrating wines across bars and restaurants; the cruise sold out and 30 percent of members signed up for a second sailing in February 2027.

Four Feathers Wine Services of Washington state developed a custom Columbia Valley brut for Holland America's fleet launched in 2024, now the most-served adult beverage across the cruise line and a significant revenue driver for their sparkling wine business.

Eleven Eleven Wines of Napa hosted 60 guests aboard Scenic Eclipse II in a seven-day Mediterranean cruise and achieved 33 percent conversion of non-members to wine club or repeat purchasers, measured through tastings, dinners, and onboard bar availability.

MARKET.head: Costco stocks boutique wines as producers struggle to sell
MARKET.summ: Sue and I recently visited our local Costco warehouse store and paused to peruse the wine aisle. We were frankly amazed at the selection we found there. It isn’t just that the prices were very good (that’s not news at Costco, where customers pay an annual membership fee).
takeaways: Costco, the largest US wine retailer, now carries boutique producer wines alongside its Kirkland Signature label despite carrying only 100-120 wines at any given time.
Producers struggling to sell wine in a surplus market are accepting placement at Costco, allowing the chain to source inventory that would rarely appear in traditional retail.
Costco's house brand model mirrors British supermarket strategy, using retailer reputation to sell unfamiliar global wines rather than relying on producer brands like US competitors do.

MARKET.head: Grape growers idle vineyards to cut costs as market demand stalls
MARKET.summ: Rather than abandoning vineyards amidst declining demand, some grape growers are pressing pause with the hopes of resuming production in a few years
takeaways: Randy Heinzen, president of Vineyard Professional Services in Paso Robles, California, notes idling is attractive because it preserves capital investment and emotional attachment to land that removal would destroy.

Proper idling requires sustained minimal irrigation, aggressive pruning, weed control, and selective pest management; inadequate care can damage vines for years, making preparation critical before returning to production.

CULTURE.head: Food-focused wine bars become James Beard, winning restaurant format globally
CULTURE.summ: When the James Beard Foundation announced its national culinary awards this summer, both the hospitality industry and the general public tuned in to see who topped the list in each category. Big winners included Los Angeles’s Kato for best wine program, Scotch Lodge in Portland, Ore., for outstanding bar, Philadelphia’s Kalaya...
takeaways: Lei, a New York wine bar that opened mid-2025, won the James Beard Foundation's best new restaurant award, marking the format's highest US honour to date.
Wine bar branding signals casual, social dining without formal pressure, allowing operators to sell wine by the glass at higher margins and serve smaller shareable plates.
The trend now spans Europe and Asia, with venues emphasizing natural and low-intervention wines, high-quality small portions, and accessible service designed to fill seats multiple times daily.

CULTURE.head: Planeta and Italian winemakers publish manifesto framing wine as contemporary culture
CULTURE.summ: A multidisciplinary meeting of the minds hosted by Planeta in 2025 gave rise to a set of guidelines to frame wine as a contemporary story, rooted in principles that have long been part of Planeta’s ethos
takeaways: Planeta, founded 30 years ago by Alessio, Francesca, and Santi Planeta in Sicily, co-authored the 2025 Manifesto di Noto with Italian winemakers, defining wine as cultural expression and common good.
The manifesto's eight principles emphasize agriculture, culture, economy, and society while centering inclusiveness, diversity, sustainability, and adaptability in wine's future.
Planeta operates five Sicilian estates and has hosted immersive experiences and art installations, positioning hospitality and storytelling as integral to contemporary wine culture.

CULTURE.head: Pink Chardonnay mutation gains traction among natural winemakers and sommeliers
CULTURE.summ: Grown in almost every major winemaking region, there are over 520,000 acres of Chardonnay vines planted around the world. The versatile white grape is notorious for its somewhat divisive nature, with expressions ranging from rich and buttery to fresh and zingy. Though the grape is ubiquitous at wine shops and restaurants,...
takeaways: Pink Chardonnay, a pink-skinned Chardonnay mutation first documented in Burgundy in the early 1900s, is produced by a handful of winemakers including Stéphane Tissot in Jura and Rajat Parr on California's Central Coast.

Champagne approved Pink Chardonnay as a permissible variety last year, and sommeliers including Tira Johnson at New York City restaurants Chez Fifi and Sushi Noz now offer single varietal expressions to diners.

Production remains tiny: Tissot yields 2,000 to 4,000 bottles annually of his Rose Massale cuvée, while Parr produces only 20 to 50 cases per vintage, limiting availability largely to direct-to-consumer sales.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Moldova is an important wine country, and increasingly it’s making some really good wines
NEWSLETTERS.summ: At a recent event in London I managed to taste through a good range of Moldovan wines. It’s one of
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jamie Goode
takeaways: Moldova has 109,700 hectares of vineyards spanning 45–49 degrees North, with 80% planted to international varieties and 20% to Caucasian and local varieties.
A tasting of recent Moldovan wines showed strong quality across producers like Château Purcari, Castel Mimi, and Vinăria Sărcuță, with multiple wines scoring 90–93 points.
Moldovan white wines emphasize local varieties (Fetească Regală, Viorica) and sparkling wines, while reds increasingly feature Fetească Neagră and Saperavi blends alongside international grapes.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Meet Your Robo-Somm
NEWSLETTERS.summ: The year is 2029. First-world civilisation has adapted to mass surveillance. Waymos and Tesla Robotaxis chauffeur NPCs between work and their domicile.
NEWSLETTERS.author: Tim Atkin MW
takeaways: Tim Atkin tested AI wine-pairing apps and found most recommend generic brands, confuse rosés with reds, and struggle with ingredient nuances and vintage variation.
SommPal, a new food and wine pairing app, ranks multiple pairings per dish with explanatory notes and identifies potential clashing factors, per developer Marc Lewin.
Atkin distinguishes between poorly-trained AI and programs developed by food and wine professionals, concluding AI pairing tools can support novice drinkers where sommeliers unavailable.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Boycott Wines Grown With Herbicides
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Putting Adam Huss’s campaign into practice at the Austrian Single Vineyard Summit
NEWSLETTERS.author: Simon J. Woolf
takeaways: Adam Huss launched a boycott campaign in August against all wines produced with herbicides, arguing they degrade soil health and decrease wine quality.
Luís Patrão from Vadio in Bairrada, Portugal reported his parents' generation's herbicide use turned vineyards into barren wastelands and eliminated local ladybird, eel, and salamander populations.
The author attended Austria's Single Vineyard Summit in Grafenegg and used producer certifications (Organic, Biodynamic, Sustainable Austria) to select only non-herbicide wines from 556 offerings.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Heading Out
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Preparing to jump to Italy next week, plus this week’s favorite stories about food, wine, and culture
NEWSLETTERS.author: Meg Maker
takeaways: Meg Maker travels to Piemonte next week to tour Roero and taste wines alongside handmade foods on a press trip with seven other American journalists.
Press tours operate with EU subsidies offsetting costs, positioning journalists as acquired product for desired media coverage rather than independent guests.
Sarah Marsh MW argues old vines aren't universally superior to young vines, noting many old vines carry viruses affecting scion and rootstock health.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Of Substack & wine
NEWSLETTERS.summ: All that’s being poured for your reading enjoyment in what is currently the most dynamic platform for wine media
NEWSLETTERS.author: Miquel Hudin
takeaways: Substack created a Wine & Spirits subsection separate from Food & Drink in its Rising and Top lists to improve discovery for wine writing.
Miquel Hudin updated the Wine Substack List (WineStack) with stricter curation criteria: publications must actively use paid subscriptions and contain only human-written text.
"Thirst Behavior" by Bodhi Landa was removed from WineStack after Substack's AI detection tools showed the majority of its text was not human-generated.
